newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian traders look for end to bourse gloom.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian traders look for end to bourse gloom.

text.p: Increased demand for bank shares on the Nigerian stock market on Friday encouraged some traders to predict the end of a gloomy period, but big conglomerates and oil marketing companies still fell.
The all-share index rose to 8437.94 from 8433.07 on Thursday.
The market has been in bearish mood for months, weighed down by economic recession, made even more damaging by recent fuel shortages.
But some dealers said on Friday they believed that the market may now be bottoming out, with companies operating at their lowest capacities but still able to survive.
They said there is a possibility of increased profits if the recession eases on increased government spending in the second half of 1997.

United Bank for Africa rose 30 kobo to 11.90 naira. NAL Merchant Bank closed at 8.30 naira, up five kobo. Guaranty Trust Bank added one kobo to 5.15 naira and Owena Bank closed two kobo higher at 1.36 naira.
Healthcare firm Smithkline Beecham gained 20 kobo to 6.00 naira and Pfizer closed 10 kobo higher at 7.35 naira.
Cappa and D'Alberto rose five kobo to 12.35 naira in a relatively quiet construction sector.
Flour Mills added 10 kobo to 18.20 naira.
Textile group Afprint got a boost from well-received full year results, rising eight kobo to 2.25 naira
But further dumping depressed the major conglomerates and petroleum marketers.
PZ Industries and Lever Brothers dropped five kobo each to 27.45 naira and 27.75 naira respectively, while UAC fell 10 kobo to 16.20 naira.
Agip fell 10 kobo to 17.20 naira and Unipetrol was 10 kobo down at 67.70 naira.
